_readme: Crop table for the plan builder. Data only — the logic lives in harvest.mjs and plan-spec.mjs.
days_to_maturity  — typical days from transplant/direct-sow to first harvest for the common
garden varieties of this crop. Seed-catalog listings cluster tightly around
these figures (Johnny's Selected Seeds, Fedco, High Mowing). Treat as a
planning estimate, not a promise: variety and season move it by weeks.
succession_days   — the usual re-sow interval for continuous harvest. From the same class of
source; a practice figure, not a measurement.
method_notes      — WHAT the method is and why. It deliberately contains NO processing times,
pressures or temperatures. Those live in the USDA/NCHFP Complete Guide to
Home Canning and must be read there, current, by the person doing the work.
Do not copy a number into this file.
companions        — widely described beneficial pairings (extension-service and permaculture
literature); presented as suggestions, not rules.

crops.name: Tomato
crops.label: tomato bed
crops.watering: Deep soak twice a week; keep leaves dry to slow blight.
crops.method_notes: The glut crop. Ripens in waves — the peak week is what the preservation plan exists for. Sauce, whole-pack, and freezing all work; the safe processing schedule is in the USDA/NCHFP Complete Guide to Home Canning.
crops.source: Johnny's Selected Seeds / Fedco catalog maturity ranges; crop notes from University of Maine Cooperative Extension bulletins on home vegetable production.

crops.name: Bush bean
crops.label: bush bean rows
crops.watering: Even moisture while flowering and podding; drought = stringy pods.
crops.method_notes: Sow every two weeks to close the gap between flushes. Freezes well and pressure-cans well; process per the USDA/NCHFP guide.
crops.source: Johnny's Selected Seeds / Fedco catalog maturity ranges; extension-service home-garden bulletins.

crops.name: Zucchini / summer squash
crops.label: zucchini hills
crops.watering: Water at the base, deeply, once or twice a week.
crops.method_notes: Two plants feed a household. Falls off a cliff if you skip two days of picking — the preservation plan's real job here is the calendar, not the recipe. Freezes for bread; safe water-bath processing per the USDA/NCHFP guide.
crops.source: Johnny's Selected Seeds / Fedco catalog maturity ranges; extension-service home-garden bulletins.

crops.name: Cucumber
crops.label: cucumber trellis
crops.watering: Consistent moisture; mulch to keep the fruit clean.
crops.method_notes: Pick every other day once it starts. Refrigerator pickles and fermented crocks are the low-effort paths; acidity and processing for shelf-stable pickles come from the USDA/NCHFP guide.
crops.source: Johnny's Selected Seeds / Fedco catalog maturity ranges; extension-service home-garden bulletins.

crops.name: Pepper
crops.label: pepper row
crops.watering: Moderate, steady water; let the soil dry between soakings.
crops.method_notes: Slow starter in cool springs — black plastic or a row cover pays for itself in Maine. Freezes superbly; roasting and freezing is more practical than canning for most households.
crops.source: Johnny's Selected Seeds / Fedco catalog maturity ranges; extension-service home-garden bulletins.

crops.name: Sweet corn
crops.label: corn block
crops.watering: Heavy drinker during tasselling and silking.
crops.method_notes: Plant in blocks, not rows, for pollination. Freezes on the cob or cut off. Everything is downhill from the moment you pick it — pick and chill fast.
crops.source: Johnny's Selected Seeds / Fedco catalog maturity ranges; extension-service home-garden bulletins.

crops.name: Beet
crops.label: beet strip
crops.watering: Even moisture; the roots get woody if they dry out.
crops.method_notes: Root cellar and clamp the fall sowing — that is the whole trick. Tops are edible; don't compost them.
crops.source: Johnny's Selected Seeds / Fedco catalog maturity ranges; extension-service home-garden bulletins.

crops.name: Carrot
crops.label: carrot rows
crops.watering: Shallow, frequent water until established, then deep weekly.
crops.method_notes: A late sowing left in the ground under mulch is the standard Maine winter-carry. Root cellar for the rest.
crops.source: Johnny's Selected Seeds / Fedco catalog maturity ranges; extension-service home-garden bulletins.

crops.name: Kale
crops.label: kale bed
crops.watering: Steady moisture; tolerates less than most brassicas.
crops.method_notes: Frost sweetens it — this is a crop to leave standing. Blanch and freeze, or carry it in the garden under cover.
crops.source: Johnny's Selected Seeds / Fedco catalog maturity ranges; extension-service home-garden bulletins.

crops.name: Garlic
crops.label: garlic bed
crops.watering: Water through spring; stop three weeks before harvest.
crops.method_notes: Planted in October, harvested the following July — the one crop you plant for next year. Cured and hung, it stores the winter; the harvest date is a calendar anchor for everything else.
crops.source: Johnny's Selected Seeds / Fedco catalog maturity ranges; extension-service home-garden bulletins.

crops.name: Onion
crops.label: onion row
crops.watering: Water until the tops fall over, then stop entirely.
crops.method_notes: Cure hard, store dry and cold, or braid. Sets versus seed matters less than curing — a badly cured onion rots in December.
crops.source: Johnny's Selected Seeds / Fedco catalog maturity ranges; extension-service home-garden bulletins.

crops.name: Potato
crops.label: potato patch
crops.watering: Even moisture through tuber set; stop as tops die back.
crops.method_notes: The storage crop by definition — the question is only whether you dig and keep or dig and eat. Cure in the dark, keep out of light.
crops.source: Johnny's Selected Seeds / Fedco catalog maturity ranges; extension-service home-garden bulletins.

crops.name: Pea
crops.label: pea trellis
crops.watering: Water at flowering; wet feet rot the vines off.
crops.method_notes: The earliest real harvest. Freezing is better than canning for texture; pick young and in the morning.
crops.source: Johnny's Selected Seeds / Fedco catalog maturity ranges; extension-service home-garden bulletins.

crops.name: Winter squash
crops.label: squash hills
crops.watering: Deep weekly water; ease off as fruit ripens.
crops.method_notes: Stores for months if cured warm and dry first — the basement is the preservation method. Two or three hills is more than enough for a household.
crops.source: Johnny's Selected Seeds / Fedco catalog maturity ranges; extension-service home-garden bulletins.

crops.name: Raspberry
crops.label: raspberry canes
crops.watering: Water during fruit set; keep the row mulched.
crops.method_notes: Year two is when it pays. Pick daily through the flush; freeze on trays and bag them, or make jam with a tested recipe.
crops.source: University of Maine Cooperative Extension small-fruit bulletins; nursery maturity guidance (nursery stock crop — first fruit the season after planting).
